home.metaDesc: SYLY answers a learner's question from the course itself, in Amharic, English or Arabic, shows the source, reads it aloud and always offers a real person.
home.h1: An accessible, multilingual assistant for every course page
home.lead: SYLY answers a learner's question from the course itself, in Amharic, English or Arabic, shows where the answer came from, reads it aloud, and always offers a real person.
home.forSub: Built first for learners who are too often left out.
home.for1p: Questions and answers in Amharic, with pre-recorded Amharic audio that works even on a phone with no Amharic voice.
home.for2p: Made for keyboard, TalkBack and NVDA, 200% zoom and 320 px width. The answer is announced without the learner moving.
home.for3p: One small script with no dependencies. It works on a slow connection, and answers already loaded work offline.
home.levelsH: Three ways to plug it in
home.levelsSub: Start with two lines. Add a server only when you need more.
home.lv1p: A script tag and a db-assistant tag. Answers come from your course text, in the browser.
home.lv2p: Adds AI answers (only if the learner allows them), a person to talk to, text messages and a Telegram bot.
home.lv3p: Marks up job posts with schema.org JobPosting, including the accommodations an employer offers.
home.how1: A learner asks a question, by typing or speaking. SYLY finds the matching part of your course.
home.how2: If the learner allows it, an AI service only puts those words into a clear sentence. It may not add anything the course does not say.
home.how3: Every answer links to the lesson section it came from.
home.how4: If nothing matches, SYLY says so and offers a real person with one button. It never guesses.
home.demoH: Try it: ask SYLY about SYLY
home.demoP: This is the real assistant, answering from a short page about SYLY. Try: What is SYLY? How does it work? Is my data private?
home.devP: Create a free developer account with Google, add your site, and get the code to paste. Learners never sign in.
home.teamP: Team SYLY (Lemi, Saron, Yabets, Yamlak) built SYLY for Track 3 of the Digital Bridge Accessibility Hackathon, ALX. The licence is to be confirmed. Everything on this site uses test data only.
privacy.lead: What SYLY stores, for learners and for developers, and how to delete it.
privacy.learn1: Questions are stored without a name or contact, only to show teachers the most asked questions (counts only).
privacy.learn2: A question goes to an online AI service only if the learner chooses Allow online answers. Nothing about who the learner is is sent. Voice notes in the Telegram bot also need this choice.
privacy.learn3: If a learner asks for a person, the request, the messages and any contact detail (a Telegram chat or a phone number) are stored. Contact details are encrypted.
privacy.learn4: A learner can download or delete everything held for them: in the assistant under Your data, in Telegram with /mydata and /delete, or by text message with STOP.
privacy.dev1: When you sign in with Google we store your Google account id (sub), your e-mail address and your name. Nothing else from Google. We ask only for openid, email and profile.
privacy.dev2: For each site you add we store its name, allowed origins, the widget settings you choose, and an optional public Telegram bot name. A site key (starting pk_) is public and goes in your page source. We store no secrets for a site.
privacy.dev3: We never receive your Telegram bot token. Keep it only in your own server's .env.
privacy.dev4: The sign-in uses one cookie, set only when you sign in. It is HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax and lasts 7 days. There are no analytics or advertising cookies.
privacy.del1: Developers: in the dashboard choose Delete my account and sites. Your account and all your sites are removed at once. Download my data gives you a JSON file first.
privacy.del2: Learners: see above. Ask the site owner if you need help.
privacy.noteP: This is a hackathon prototype. Use test data only; do not enter real personal information. The licence is to be confirmed.
signin.lead: For people who add SYLY to a website. Learners never need to sign in.
signin.why: You sign in with your Google account. We ask only for your Google account id, e-mail address and name (openid, email, profile). We keep them to show your sites. See Privacy.
signin.btnHelp: The next control is Google's own button. If you cannot reach it with the keyboard or your screen reader, use the button after it, which opens Google's quick sign-in prompt instead.
signin.promptHelp: If nothing appears, your browser may have hidden the prompt. Reload the page and try again.
signin.after: After you sign in you go to your dashboard.
signin.notConfigured: Sign-in is not configured on this server. Every other page works. The team lead can set it up: see Google sign-in setup in the README.
signin.checking: Checking whether you are already signed in…
signin.gisFail: Google's sign-in could not be loaded. Check your connection and reload the page.
docs.metaDesc: Install SYLY, every attribute, events, the REST API, content sources, the Telegram bot, bring your own bot, accessibility and privacy.
docs.lead: Everything you need to add the SYLY assistant to your site. Use the assistant on this page to ask about it: it reads this page.
docs.instP: Three ways to load the same file. Put the script tag and the db-assistant tag before the closing body tag of your page.
docs.inst1P: Use the address of the server that runs SYLY (yours or ours).
docs.inst2P: jsDelivr serves the file from the public GitHub repository, pinned to a version tag. The api and content attributes must be full https:// addresses, because a CDN does not know where your server is.
docs.inst3P: Install the package, then import it, or add a script tag that points into node_modules. The package has no dependencies.
docs.inst3Note: The package is ready, but it is published only by the team lead with an npm account. Until then use the server or CDN version.
docs.instGen: You can also build the tag with options and a live preview on the install page.
docs.a_lang: Language of the assistant: am, en, ar, or any file module/i18n/CODE.json.
docs.a_api: Base URL of the SYLY server, for example https://your-host/api. Empty: the assistant works alone with keyword search in the browser.
docs.a_content: URL of a bilingual content file. Empty: the server's sections, then page reading.
docs.a_site: Your site key from the dashboard (pk_…). The assistant loads your saved settings from the server. Attributes on the tag always win. Needs api.
docs.a_theme: auto uses the host page's --bs-primary only if it passes 4.5:1 with white, otherwise a safe navy.
docs.a_mode: panel: a button on the side edge opens a full-height panel. inline: the ask box sits in the page.
docs.a_position: Which edge the panel button sits on.
docs.a_primary: One colour as six hex digits, for example #1A5FB4. Ignored if it does not pass 4.5:1 with white.
docs.a_selector: CSS selector of the lesson on your page, for page reading, for example #lesson.
docs.a_readpage: Page reading: empty (only when there is no content file or server section), always (the page is added to the content file), off.
docs.evP: All events bubble and are composed, so you can listen on document.
docs.evMethods: Methods on the element: open(), close(), ask(text), openAccommodation({id, title}), showJobAlerts(keyword), getText(key, lang).
docs.apiP: Every call is under /api/v1. The interactive documentation lets you try each one. Errors always come as {"detail": "words"}.
docs.r_ask: Answer a question from the course, with sources.
docs.r_content: The indexed sections. POST: your site sends its lessons to be indexed.
docs.r_config: What the widget needs to know at start.
docs.r_esc: Talk to a person: open a ticket, then send and poll messages.
docs.r_voice: Text to speech and speech to text (these send text or audio online, so they need the learner's consent).
docs.r_jobs: Test jobs with schema.org JobPosting, job alerts and interview-support requests.
docs.r_sites: Developer portal: the public widget settings for a site key. The rest needs a sign-in.
docs.contentP: The assistant uses the first source that has content.
docs.c1: A content file (the content attribute): sections with id, url, title_en/am, text_en/am and keywords_en/am.
docs.c2: Sections held by the server for this page (POST /api/v1/content).
docs.c3: Page reading: the assistant reads the lesson on your page itself (headings h2 and h3), ignoring navigation, hidden parts, forms and ads. Nothing is stored. Use content-selector to point at the lesson.
docs.botP: Every command works by tapping the menu, by typing a short phrase, or by sending a voice note. Longer messages are questions.
docs.botLangP: The interface and phrases are drafts that need a native reader check. Speech recognition quality differs a lot by language.
docs.l_am: Done. Typed Amharic works fully; spoken Amharic is weak until Addis AI has credit.
docs.l_ar: Beta. Speech recognition works well on test clips.
docs.byobP: Each college runs SYLY with its own bot. SYLY never receives your bot token.
docs.byob1: Open @BotFather in Telegram, send /newbot, then choose a name and a username that ends in bot.
docs.byob2: Copy the token BotFather gives you.
docs.byob3: Put it in your own server's .env file as TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN.
docs.byob4: Start the bot with docker compose up -d bot.
docs.byob5: Optional: send /setuserpic and /setdescription to BotFather to add your logo and a description.
docs.byob6: The commands and phrases register themselves when the bot starts.
docs.byobWarn: Never paste your bot token into a website or a chat. Keep it only in your server's .env.
docs.byobUser: In the dashboard you can save the bot's public username (for example @MyCollegeHelpBot). It is not secret; it is used only to show the right link in your generated code.
docs.a11yP: SYLY is built to WCAG 2.2 AA: real elements, visible focus, 44 px targets, 200% zoom, 320 px width, no time limits. Automated checks pass. Manual tests with TalkBack, NVDA and a co-designer are still pending, and the statement says so honestly.
docs.a11yGoogle: The Google sign-in button is Google's own iframe. We add a text explanation and a skip link, but we cannot change its internals.
docs.privP: Learners are never asked to sign in, questions are stored without names, and online AI is used only with the learner's consent.
